label: Person
name: Visconte Maggiolo
summary:
Visconte Maggiolo was a prominent Genoese cartographer who made significant contributions to the field of nautical charting during the Renaissance. His most notable work, 'Carta Marina', provided detailed information about coastal geography and marine navigation, showcasing his expertise in mapping the Mediterranean region.

Born around 1500, Visconte Maggiolo was a prominent figure in Genoa's maritime community, collaborating with other notable cartographers such as Francesco Bertolini. His work built upon earlier efforts by cartographers like Paolo dal Pozzo Toscanelli, expanding our understanding of the world's oceans and coastlines.

Maggiolo's legacy extends beyond his own work, influencing later generations of cartographers and marine explorers. His maps served as a reference point for sailors and traders, helping to establish Genoa as a major hub in the Mediterranean trade network.

A lasting testament to Maggiolo's impact is the continued use of his 'Carta Marina' by historians and scholars today, offering valuable insights into the world of 16th-century cartography. His contributions demonstrate the importance of accurate mapping during this period, shaping the course of maritime history and global trade.
